title: 1.3 Plate Movements and Plate Boundaries
description: Convergent, divergent and transform boundaries, subduction, seafloor spreading and mantle convection. Hard level.

questions.question: How does subduction produce volcanoes in the Andes?
options: Subducted crust melts and the magma rises through the overlying crust
The plate pushes mountains upward without melting
Ocean water cools the mantle into lava
Wind erosion exposes molten rock
questions.correctAnswer: Subducted crust melts and the magma rises through the overlying crust

questions.question: Why do two continental plates build mountains rather than subduct deeply?
options: Continental crust is denser than the mantle
Continental crust is buoyant and resists sinking
Continental crust melts completely
Continental crust is thinner than oceanic crust
questions.correctAnswer: Continental crust is buoyant and resists sinking

questions.question: What distinguishes an oceanic ridge from a continental rift valley?
options: A ridge forms on land; a rift forms only in the ocean
Both are transform features
A ridge forms undersea by seafloor spreading; a rift forms on a continent
Both are subduction features
questions.correctAnswer: A ridge forms undersea by seafloor spreading; a rift forms on a continent

questions.question: How does the East African Rift illustrate an early stage of ocean formation?
options: It is already a deep ocean basin
It will become a mountain range
It is a transform fault that will close
Continued separation may let water flood the gap to form a new ocean
questions.correctAnswer: Continued separation may let water flood the gap to form a new ocean

questions.question: Why do transform boundaries produce earthquakes?
options: Plates stick and then slip suddenly along fractures
Plates melt and recrystallize
Plates move apart very quickly
Plates form new crust continuously
questions.correctAnswer: Plates stick and then slip suddenly along fractures

questions.question: Where do rising and descending convection currents occur?
options: Rising at subduction zones and descending at ridges
Rising at oceanic ridges and descending at subduction zones
Rising beneath continents only
Descending beneath deserts only
questions.correctAnswer: Rising at oceanic ridges and descending at subduction zones

questions.question: What determines whether plates converge, diverge or slide past one another?
options: Their color and age
The salinity of nearby seas
The direction of their relative motion at the margin
The number of fossils they contain
questions.correctAnswer: The direction of their relative motion at the margin

questions.question: What happens to crustal material at subduction zones?
options: It is preserved unchanged
It becomes new oceanic crust at the surface
It turns into sedimentary rock immediately
It is destroyed and recycled into the mantle
questions.correctAnswer: It is destroyed and recycled into the mantle

questions.question: Why does oceanic-oceanic convergence form an island arc?
options: Subduction of one oceanic plate beneath another builds volcanic islands
Two continents collide and uplift
Seafloor spreading creates a ridge
A transform fault opens a gap
questions.correctAnswer: Subduction of one oceanic plate beneath another builds volcanic islands

questions.question: Which sequence correctly links convergence to volcanism?
options: Convergence, erosion, sedimentation, volcano
Convergence, subduction, melting, magma rise, volcano
Divergence, cooling, sinking, volcano
Transform motion, melting, volcano
questions.correctAnswer: Convergence, subduction, melting, magma rise, volcano
